text:
alexa: FYI saw a weird terraform plan in staging that wants to replace namespace labels and taint two secrets. I didn't change infra today, opened this thread to see if anyone else noticed.

mason: can you paste the plan snippet?

alexa: here's the relevant bit from the plan:```
# kubernetes_namespace.myapp will be updated in-place
~ metadata[0].labels["env"] = "staging" -> "staging"

# kubernetes_secret.db-creds must be replaced
-/+ resource "kubernetes_secret" "db-creds" {
    ~ data = { ... } -> (known after apply)
  }
```

ravi: hmm, labels look identical. Could be provider schema change mapping null->empty map or ordering diff. We had the k8s provider bump in the last infra deploy.

ci-bot: provider upgrade applied to staging: registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/kubernetes v2.14.0 -> v2.15.0 (migration: label normalization)

sam: @mason @ravi I've seen this before — terraform treats map ordering/empty values as a diff after provider changes. Usually a targeted refresh fixes it: `terraform refresh -target=kubernetes_namespace.myapp -target=kubernetes_secret.db-creds` then re-run plan.

mason: quick check — what does `terraform state show kubernetes_namespace.myapp` show for metadata.labels?

alexa: state shows `labels = { "env" = "staging" }` and cluster shows `kubectl get ns myapp -o yaml` -> `labels: { env: staging }`. So identical, but plan still wants update.

ravi: did we import any resources manually recently? Imported resources sometimes leave provider references pointing to old provider block. Run `terraform state replace-provider` if provider namespace changed.

mason: running a local refresh now. If it's a provider-schema normalization, the plan will flip once we refresh to the new provider shape. Will report.

alexa: also the secrets being replaced worries me — they contain short-lived tokens. We should avoid apply until we confirm.

sam: If refresh doesn't help, another safe workaround is to add an explicit lifecycle ignore_changes on `metadata[0].labels` for a short window, but that's risky. Prefer find root cause.

ravi: check if any modules set `data = {}` vs `null` for secret data; provider change may treat empty map differently and force replacement. Also check `sensitive` computed fields in secret resources.

mason: refresh done locally — plan no longer shows namespace label update, but secrets still marked replace. Running `kubectl get secret db-creds -n myapp -o json` to compare.

alexa: cluster secret has annotations `managed-by: external-sync` — could be external controller recreating fields. If controller rewrites secret fields, TF will detect drift and try to replace.

ravi: good catch. If external-sync updates `data` (or adds immutable fields), TF will replace. Is the secret immutable? `kubectl get secret db-creds -n myapp -o yaml | grep immutable`

sam: also check if secret is created by a kustomize overlay in the deployment pipeline. We had a rollout last night that touched secrets in staging.

mason: `kubectl` shows `immutable: true` for that secret. That explains replacement — TF cannot update immutable secrets and will recreate. Why did immutable get set? audit logs?

deploy-bot: deploy pipeline completed: staging/app-sync from commit 4f3a2b — included kustomize secret manifest with `immutable: true`.

alexa: so sequence: pipeline applied immutable=true, TF sees drift and plans replacement -> wants to delete/create secret (replacement) -> taint risk for app. We need to coordinate.

ravi: plan: 1) hold TF apply in staging until we coordinate with deploy owners; 2) if secret must be immutable, import current secret state into TF with the immutable flag so plan stops flipping (or manage secret outside TF); 3) avoid destroy/recreate by letting kustomize manage secret, and remove secret resource from TF state (terraform state rm) if we choose that.

sam: I can ping the deploy team to revert immutable flag for staging (non-prod) if they don't need it. @alexa can you hold the apply?

alexa: holding. I've cancelled the apply job and put a note in the run.

mason: I'll open a tiny PR to either align TF resource with current secret manifest or to remove secret from TF state. Will link here when ready.

alexa: thanks. 🙏 Also good to add a short runbook for secrets that are managed by kustomize vs terraform — avoid dual write.

ravi: agree. I'll draft a one-pager and drop in #eng-infra later today.

mason: PR: https://git.internal.redwood/pr/4823 — sets `immutable = true` on the TF secret resource to match cluster. planning now looks clean.

alexa: re-running targeted plan shows only the secret unchanged. Good. Thanks everyone.

sam: :thumbsup:

mason: I'll coordinate with deploy owners tomorrow to ensure manifests don't flip flags randomly. Closing this thread unless anyone objects.

alexa: no objections. thanks all.
